audit_findings.title: Plant-closure cash claim is not visibly reconciled
audit_findings.magnitude: $64.7 million provision at June 30, 2026; 112% of $57.6 million anchor OE, 6.1% of $1,059 million base equity value, or $2.47 per share if fully deducted
audit_findings.mechanism: Future closure payments either reduce forecast OE when paid or require a separate deduction from the cash bridge; omitting both treatments overstates equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: Plant closure provisions at December 31, 2025 amounted to $65.1 million and relate principally to asset retirement obligations at our Ellesmere Port site in the U.K..
audit_findings.explanation: The obligation and its size are demonstrated, but double counting is unresolved because historical cash OE already includes cash utilization of provisions. The filing shows $2.1 million utilized in the first half of 2026 and $5.8 million in 2025, while the remaining $64.7 million provision is larger than one year of anchor OE. A full deduction would be material, although the correct adjustment is only the portion not already captured in forecast OE.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $64.7 million June 2026 provision by settlement year against closure cash payments embedded in each forecast year, then rerun all scenarios with only the uncovered present value deducted.

audit_findings.title: Not all bridge cash may be distributable surplus
audit_findings.magnitude: $131.4 million held by non-U.S. subsidiaries, equal to 52.5% of $250.2 million bridge cash, 12.4% of base equity value, or $5.02 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Unavailable cash must be excluded from the equity bridge because portfolio interest income was removed from OE and the entire cash balance was then added separately.
audit_findings.evidence: As at December 31, 2025 and 2024, we had cash and cash equivalents of $292.5 million and $289.2 million, respectively, of which $145.4 million and $133.9 million, respectively, were held by non-U.S. subsidiaries principally in the U.K..
audit_findings.explanation: The valuation demonstrably adds gross cash, but the record does not demonstrate that the $131.4 million held outside the U.S. is restricted or subject to incremental tax. Minimum operating cash is also unquantified. The identified exposure is sufficiently large to be material if a significant portion is unavailable.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the June 2026 legal-entity cash schedule, trapped-cash restrictions, repatriation taxes and minimum operating-cash analysis; rerun the bridge using only distributable surplus cash and avoid duplicating any recorded deferred tax liability.

audit_findings.title: Terminal growth may omit the scheduled AvGas runoff
audit_findings.mechanism: An AvGas decline would reduce forecast OE, growth and terminal OE and could add shutdown or remediation cash outflows.
audit_findings.evidence: The most significant announcement impacting the Company is the stated aim of EAGLE to eliminate lead emissions from general aviation in the U.S. by the end of 2030 with Alaska having a derogation out to end 2032.
audit_findings.explanation: This is principally a forward-looking displacement risk rather than a demonstrated model error. The filing provides no AvGas revenue, margin or OE dollars, so its valuation effect cannot be measured. Current indicators warrant attention: AvGas sales declined 5% and volume declined 12% in the first half of 2026, while second-quarter sales declined 21%. The planned 2030 phaseout also overlaps the model's fade toward 2.5% perpetual growth.
audit_findings.action: Obtain AvGas revenue, contribution margin, sustaining capital and closure-cost forecasts through 2032; then rerun each scenario with explicit runoff and replacement-business assumptions before relying on terminal growth.

audit_findings.title: The 2025 anchor requires proof that a discrete tax benefit was removed
audit_findings.magnitude: $9.5 million, equal to 16.5% of anchor OE; if embedded, approximately $133.4 million or $5.10 per share of base operating value
audit_findings.mechanism: A noncash tax credit retained in anchor OE would be compounded through forecast OE and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: While the change in estimate had no impact on pre-tax income, it has resulted in the recognition of a deferred tax asset of $ 9.5 million and a credit to net income of $ 9.5 million for the twelve months ended December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The $9.5 million nonrecurring benefit is demonstrated, but its inclusion in the $57.6 million anchor is not. The cash-flow statement's $10.2 million deferred-tax reversal suggests a cash-based OE calculation may already remove it, but the exact OE reconciliation is absent. Because operating value scales with the anchor, confirmed inclusion would be material.
audit_findings.action: Produce the line-by-line 2025 OE reconciliation showing the $9.5 million credit and related deferred-tax reversal; if any portion remains, remove it and rerun all scenarios without altering recurring tax expense.

audit_findings.title: Deferred acquisition consideration is a non-debt claim on cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $4.1 million at June 30, 2026, equal to 0.4% of $1,059 million base equity value or $0.16 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Unpaid acquisition consideration is a direct claim on bridge cash and should be deducted unless explicitly modeled as a forecast cash outflow.
audit_findings.evidence: A portion of the consideration is deferred and payable in cash by December 7, 2026, and contingent on the financial performance of QGP for the 12 months ended June 30, 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The omission is demonstrated if the bridge truly adds gross cash without recognizing this claim, but its current filed amount is too small to alter the conclusion. Deducting the full $4.1 million would reduce base value from about $40.48 to $40.32 per share, still far below the $93.95 market price.
audit_findings.action: Deduct the filed $4.1 million from bridge cash, or document the matching forecast cash outflow; update the amount when the QGP settlement is finalized.

audit_findings.title: Consolidated cash-flow inputs may not fully match the common-share denominator
audit_findings.mechanism: NCI-attributable operating cash flow could overstate common OE, while NCI-attributable capital expenditure or working-capital investment could understate it; any net error could affect the historical series, anchor and growth judgment.
audit_findings.evidence: The consolidated financial statements have been prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles (“GAAP”) in the United States of America on a going concern basis and include all subsidiaries of the Company where the Company has a controlling financial interest.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing confirms noncontrolling interests—$2.4 million of 2024 income and $4.9 million of year-end NCI equity—but does not provide subsidiary-level cash-flow attribution. The reported greater-than-5% FY2024 gap is therefore an unresolved possibility rather than a demonstrated OE error. A FY2024-only correction would not replace the lower $57.6 million latest-year anchor under the MIN rule, but similar mismatches in 2025 could affect value materially.
audit_findings.action: Trace operating cash flow, D&A, capital expenditure and working-capital movements for each partially owned subsidiary for every OE year; compute common-equity OE and rerun only if the corrected 2025 anchor or selected trend changes.
